summary: MarsMate is a web platform that gives astronauts a single, layered view of the Martian surface for planning and conducting a Marswalk. Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript and live NASA Mars Trek data, it combines optical, thermal, topographic and mission imagery — including Viking, MOC, THEMIS, MOLA and HiRISE — over real landing sites and rover traverses at Jezero Crater and Gale Crater's Mount Sharp, where Curiosity observed boxwork formations in 2025. Explorers can switch basemaps, stack data layers, follow waypoints along a route, and inspect the same terrain in 2D or as a 3D planet. By integrating data from multiple NASA missions instead of separate maps, MarsMate helps crews choose safer routes, avoid obstacles, and target the most valuable science sites. It turns scattered Mars data into one clear, usable view for the next generation of human exploration.
details:
What MarsMate does

MarsMate is a web platform that gives astronauts a single, layered view of the Martian surface for planning and conducting a Marswalk. It focuses on two real sites: Jezero Crater, explored by Perseverance, and Gale Crater / Mount Sharp, explored by Curiosity, including the boxwork formations Curiosity observed there in 2025.

How it works

MarsMate streams live map tiles directly from NASA's Mars Trek. Users can switch between 6 basemaps — Viking colour, MOC Atlas, THEMIS Day Infrared, MOLA colour relief, MOLA + HRSC relief, and MOLA elevation — and stack overlays with opacity controls, including THEMIS Night Infrared, HiRISE and CTX mosaics. It also shows all 9 NASA landing sites, a lat/lon grid, live cursor coordinates, waypoints along a rover traverse, and the same terrain as a rotatable 3D planet built from the same Trek tiles. All imagery and terrain data comes from real NASA missions. No data is made up.

Main use case

An explorer preparing a Marswalk at Mount Sharp opens MarsMate, selects Gale Crater, and switches to MOLA relief to check elevation and slopes. They add THEMIS thermal imagery to compare warm and cold terrain, then add the HiRISE mosaic to see surface detail and possible obstacles. They follow the waypoints along the traverse toward the boxwork area, switch to the 3D view to understand the terrain in context, and use that combined view to choose a safer route to the most valuable science target.

Benefits and intended impact

Instead of checking separate maps and mission archives, an explorer sees optical, thermal, and topographic data together in one view. That makes it faster to compare terrain, spot obstacles, and choose a route that is both safe and scientifically valuable. MarsMate is built to support future human exploration on Mars, help crews make better decisions on the surface, and make real Mars science more accessible to students, researchers, and the public.

Tools, languages, and software used

HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Leaflet for the 2D layered map and Three.js for the 3D planet globe. Data from JPL Mars Trek, the USGS-NASA Planetary Geologic Mapping Program, NASA Worldview, the Mars Perseverance Raw Images Gallery, and Curiosity's route map for lower Mount Sharp. No backend and no special hardware were used — it runs entirely in a modern web browser and is hosted on GitHub Pages.

Working features — delivered now

Layered 2D Mars Trek map with 6 basemaps and stackable overlays, 3D planet view, 9 landing sites, waypoints and traverse line, lat/lon grid and live coordinates, and full-page map mode.

Limitations

MarsMate needs an internet connection to load live Trek tiles. Waypoint positions along traverses are approximate where the source data is approximate. It does not include live radiation, space weather, or spacesuit telemetry, and it is not flight software.

Future plans — not yet delivered

Offline tile caching, a radiation and space-weather overlay, automatic slope and traversability analysis, and annotated science targets for boxwork and other formations.
